title: Fraction Remainder Problems
topic: Fraction of Remainder and Multi-Step Problems
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: Alice spent 1/3 of her money on books and 1/2 of the remainder on food. What fraction of her original money was left?
questions.explanation: After books: 1 - 1/3 = 2/3 left. Food: 1/2 of 2/3 = 1/3. Total spent: 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3. Left: 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.

questions.question: Ben had some stamps. He gave 1/4 to his brother and 2/5 of the remainder to his sister. What fraction of his original stamps did he have left?
Tom saved some money. He spent 1/3 on toys, then $24 on snacks. He was left with exactly 2/5 of his original savings. How much did he save at first?
Dan had $200. He spent 1/5 on food and 3/4 of the remainder on transport. How much money did he have left?
questions.explanation: After food: 200 × 4/5 = $160 left. Transport: 3/4 of 160 = $120. Left: 160 - 120 = $40.

questions.question: A bag contains some marbles. 3/8 are red. 1/4 of the remainder are blue. The rest are 45 green marbles. How many marbles are in the bag?
There were 210 students in a hall. 3/7 were boys and 1/4 of the girls wore glasses. How many girls did not wear glasses?
questions.explanation: Boys: 210 × 3/7 = 90. Girls: 210 - 90 = 120. Girls with glasses: 120 × 1/4 = 30. Girls without glasses: 120 - 30 = 90.

questions.question: Maya spent $35 on a dress and 2/5 of the remainder on shoes. She had $24 left. How much money did she have at first?
questions.explanation: After shoes, she had 3/5 of the remainder left. 3/5 rem = $24 → 1/5 rem = $8 → full rem = $40. Original = Dress + Remainder = 35 + 40 = $75.

questions.question: Grace used 1/8 of her flour for cakes and 3/7 of the remainder for cookies. What fraction of her original flour was left?
questions.explanation: After cakes: 1 - 1/8 = 7/8 left. Cookies: 3/7 of 7/8 = 3/8. Total used: 1/8 + 3/8 = 1/2. Left: 1 - 1/2 = 1/2.

questions.question: Ivy ate 1/5 of a cake and gave 1/2 of the remainder to her friend. What fraction of the original cake was left?
questions.explanation: After ate: 1 - 1/5 = 4/5 left. Friend: 1/2 of 4/5 = 2/5. Total gone: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5. Left: 1 - 3/5 = 2/5.

questions.question: Mr. Tan gave 1/4 of his apples to his neighbour. He then gave 2/5 of the remainder to his son. The remaining apples were shared equally among his 3 daughters, and each received 18 apples. How many apples did he have at first?
questions.explanation: After son: 3/5 of 3/4 = 9/20 left. Shared by 3 daughters → each gets 3/20. 3/20 = 18 → 1/20 = 6. Total (20/20) = 6 × 20 = 120.

questions.question: Jack spent 1/7 of his money on books and 1/2 of the remainder on food. What fraction of his original money was left?
questions.explanation: After books: 1 - 1/7 = 6/7 left. Food: 1/2 of 6/7 = 3/7. Total spent: 1/7 + 3/7 = 4/7. Left: 1 - 4/7 = 3/7.

questions.question: Sarah spent $30 on lunch. She then spent 1/4 of the remainder on stationery. She was left with exactly 1/3 of her original money. How much did she have at first?
questions.explanation: After stationery, 3/4 of the remainder was left. 3/4(Original - 30) = 1/3 Original. Cross-multiply: 9(Original - 30) = 4Original → 5Original = 270 → Original = $54.

questions.question: There were 560 marbles in a bag. 1/7 were green and 2/3 of the remainder were yellow. How many marbles were neither green nor yellow?
A school had 600 students. 1/4 were in Primary 6 and 1/2 of the remainder were in Primary 5. How many students were in neither Primary 6 nor Primary 5?
A water tank was 3/4 full. 1/5 of the water in the tank was drained. Then 12 litres were added, and the tank became exactly full. What is the capacity of the tank?
questions.explanation: Drained = 1/5 of 3/4 = 3/20. Left = 3/4 - 3/20 = 12/20 = 3/5. Added 12 L fills to 1. So 12 L = 2/5 capacity. 1/5 = 6 L. Full capacity = 5 × 6 = 30 L.

questions.question: Leo spent 3/10 of his money on a toy and 1/3 of the remainder on candy. What fraction of his original money was left?
Kelly used 1/5 of her ribbon for a gift and 3/4 of the remainder for a craft. What fraction of her original ribbon was left?
questions.explanation: After gift: 1 - 1/5 = 4/5 left. Craft: 3/4 of 4/5 = 3/5. Total used: 1/5 + 3/5 = 4/5. Left: 1 - 4/5 = 1/5.

questions.question: A farmer had 450 chickens. He sold 1/3 of them and gave 1/5 of the remainder to his neighbour. How many chickens did he have left?
questions.explanation: After sold: 450 × 2/3 = 300 left. Neighbour: 1/5 of 300 = 60. Left: 300 - 60 = 240.

questions.question: There were 360 pencils in a box. 1/3 were red and 3/5 of the remainder were blue. How many pencils were neither red nor blue?
A shop had 400 shirts. They sold 1/4 in the morning and 1/3 of the remainder in the afternoon. How many shirts were left?
questions.explanation: After morning: 400 × 3/4 = 300 left. Afternoon: 1/3 of 300 = 100. Left: 300 - 100 = 200.
